editorApprovedScope.userApproval: User answered Yes to assessing the main Jonathan Sacks–Richard Dawkins conversation before audience questions, excluding substantive moderator interventions and directly dependent replies, with reader-facing scope disclosure. Exact boundaries remain to be verified.
editorApprovedScope.requiredReaderDisclosure: This assessment covers selected, self-contained Jonathan Sacks–Richard Dawkins exchanges within the main conversation, approximately 2:09–41:54. Substantive moderator interventions and their dependent replies are excluded, removing approximately 20:31 (51.6%) of that window and leaving approximately 19:14 of eligible conversation. The exclusions include host-led exchanges about book tone, selective evidence, divine intervention, religious upbringing, antisemitism, and moral necessity. Introductions and all audience Q&A are also unscored. Neither speaker receives credit or penalty for excluded material; the scores do not assess the complete event.

excludedIntervals.reason: The moderator introduces the accusation of aggressive, jeering confrontation and Dawkins answers that characterization. Exclude the complete tone discussion and immediate follow-up; retain his subsequent explicit return to Sacks's independently stated how/why distinction.

The moderator states that religious thinkers opportunistically invoke evidence but claim an opt-out when it is absent. Exclude this substantive framing and Dawkins's full immediate reply, including the connected DNA explanation; neither side receives credit or penalty for this exchange.

The moderator presses the relevance to science and the factual occurrence of divine intervention. Exclude the whole continuous host-led branch, Sacks's power-of-the-powerless explanation, Dawkins's denial of the event, and the conditional rejoinder. Resume only at Dawkins's new Adam-and-Eve question.

The moderator advances the counterexample that increasing numbers read scripture literally. Exclude her claim and Sacks's dependent oral-tradition/heresy reply. The following neutral request about Abraham and Isaac is a fresh topic prompt, not an argument supplied by the moderator.

Conservatively exclude the uninterrupted chain beginning with the moderator's teacher/obedience anecdote, followed by the Christian-reading and antisemitism dispute, compulsory-belief/faith-school framing, admissions and quasi-racial identity objections, and the claimed need for religion to supply ethics. Exclude all directly dependent answers and rebuttals, including both sides' replies on moral necessity. Resume at Sacks's separately introduced empirical Putnam evidence, which supplies its own warrant without requiring the excluded premise.

Sacks explicitly recapitulates the excluded claim that religion is not needed to know what to do; the moderator then proposes a Darwinian-survival inference. Exclude that dependent concession, its connected ritual gloss, the host inference, and the overlapping immediate reactions. Dawkins's separate methodological question about the independently retained Putnam evidence is eligible afterward.

Dawkins expressly invokes his earlier, excluded century/decade argument; Sacks responds by discussing religion's resistance to the zeitgeist. Exclude this entire dependent exchange so an omitted argument supplies neither a scored premise nor a scored rebuttal. Resume when Dawkins explicitly returns to the independently retained community mechanism.

editorApprovedScope.boundaryBasis: Complete original upload transcribed in timestamp-preserving chunks, two cross-boundary sentences independently verified, and all source speech reviewed against the official publisher transcript. The opening substantive case starts at 129.200 seconds; the final complete main-conversation reply ends at 2513.720 seconds, immediately before the invitation to audience questions.
editorApprovedScope.outsideWindowDisposition: Unscored introduction and pleasantries before the opening substantive case; all audience questions and answers excluded. The recording itself ends during a final Q&A answer.
editorApprovedScope.coherenceReview: Retained exchanges contain their own premises: scientific partnership and cosmic purpose, symbolic/literal readings, Abraham and Isaac, independently introduced empirical community evidence and its methodological challenge, prospective secular community, religious persistence, and closing common ground. Dependent chains are excluded conservatively; no omitted rebuttal may be treated as silence.
